title: ÆTHER: Tisram (Carnatic EDM, the rhythm changes gear)
maker: ElevenLabs Music API on the owner's paid plan

positive_styles: a huge modern festival EDM track built on Carnatic classical rhythm: driving tech-house and drum & bass energy at 128 BPM, punchy kick, deep rolling bass, massive bright synths, wide modern mix
the melody is Carnatic raga Kiravani in G#: G# A# B C# D# E G, phrased like a Carnatic singer with slides and fast gamakam ornaments, each repeat of the hook more ornamented (sangathi)
a powerful Carnatic-trained female voice sings the hook in swara syllables (sa ri ga ma pa da ni) and climbs to ringing high notes
real Carnatic percussion played by real musicians, close and natural: mridangam, kanjira, ghatam, thavil; Carnatic violin and veena; tanpura drone on G# and D#
THE IDEA: the rhythm changes gear (nadai): straight 4 (chatusram) suddenly switches to triplets (tisram) and back, like a Carnatic percussionist, every switch a surprise
hype every few seconds, euphoric, goosebumps
second 0: the full band hits a loud 3-against-4 triplet figure on mridangam and synth stabs, then the voice snaps in on a high note

brief.notes: Jithesh 3 Nov 08:44 'yes next' after Tara posted. Album track 2. Conditioned on Tara take 1 (28-58 s, first drop) so the album shares one sound. Device: nadai change (chatusram <-> tisram switches) as the hype moment, korvai builds/ending, tani breakdown. Kiravani G# (Tara landed in G#), 128 BPM, 2:30.

story: Same festival, later that night. The drummers take over: every time the beat flips into triplets, the crowd loses its footing and screams for more.
